Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller or simpler version of the same problem. Each recursive function needs a *base case*, which is a simple situation it can answer directly without calling itself again. With each call, the problem gets closer to the base case, until the base case is reached and the calls can start returning answers. You can think of it like a stack of plates: each recursive call adds a plate, and once you reach the bottom (the base case), you start removing plates one by one as the results are returned.
